# Fiction tells (dated)

last_verified: 2026-11-17, from the owner's tells list (StoryScope, Hamilton and Mimno, Infinity-Chat) and `research_notes/`.
Re-check: names and phrases every 3 months, plot-shape findings every 6 months, everything after a major model release.

A tell is a reason to rework a passage. It is never proof of who wrote it. One tell means nothing; several kinds together mean the draft ran on defaults.

## Structure (strongest, slowest to expire)

| Tell | Fix |
|---|---|
| One plot line, no subplot (79% of AI stories vs 57% of human, StoryScope, Apr 2026) | Give a minor character a want that runs against the lead's, or add a time jump |
| Narrator or character states the theme (77% vs 52%) | Cut the line. Let an object or action carry it |
| Ends on internal acceptance (47% vs 27%) | Stop one beat earlier. End unresolved, ironic or slightly wrong |
| Emotion shown only through body sensation (81% vs 38%) | Name some feelings plainly. Show others through behavior |
| Dialogue used to debate the theme (59% vs 34%) | Make each line want something, dodge or interrupt |
| Hero's choice is obviously right, outcome is neat | Make the choice cost something. Leave one thing unmet |
| Flat escalation (Claude-leaning) | Raise the stakes each scene |
| Dream sequences (GPT-leaning) | Cut, or replace with a real event |
| Characters described only by looks (Gemini-leaning) | Give habits, speech, what they avoid |
| Every speaker calm, articulate and wise | Give each a rhythm, wrong words, fragments. Swap test: could names be swapped? |
| Same premise as everyone's | Change the premise, not the nouns (Infinity-Chat, 2025) |

## Names, settings, phrases (expire fast)

- **Stock names:** Elara, Elias, Kael, Lyra, Thorne, Mara, Aria, Luna, Seraphina. 11 words, including these names and jobs, appeared in 88.3% of 20,000 stories from four models (Hamilton and Mimno, arXiv 2605.26492, May 2026; preprint, cause unconfirmed). Fix: choose culture, era and family first, then the name.
- **Stock settings and jobs:** lighthouse keeper, clockmaker, librarian, baker, small coastal town, old shop. Fix: a place you can describe with three unexpected objects.
- **Stock phrases:** "a shiver ran down", "the air was thick with", "little did they know", "a testament to", "whispers of", "tapestry", "in that moment, they understood", "heart pounded". Fix: say what happened, with one concrete detail.
- **Openers:** weather, or "in a small town where everyone knew everyone". Fix: start in the scene.
- **Triplets** of adjectives or actions in every sentence. Fix: use the real count.
- **Poems:** abstract nouns ("the weight of silence"), a moral last stanza, forced rhyme. Practitioner observation, no 2025+ study. Fix: one touchable object; cut the last stanza and re-read.

## Guards

- Many tells are common in human beginner fiction and genre fiction too. Judge the passage, never the writer.
- A parody, a quotation or a deliberate cliche in a character's mouth is exempt.
- Reader tests of AI poetry are old (2024, one older model); do not lean on them.
- Per-model quirks come from one preprint with some AI-labeled features. Treat as leads.
- Lists are English-language and drift as models change.

- Hamilton and Mimno, arXiv 2605.26492, 26 May 2026; Cornell Chronicle, 19 Oct 2026.
